Umrah expiates the sins since the last one; Umrah before Hajj is no harm; the Prophet's four Umrahs, none in Rajab and mostly in Dhul-Qa'da; Umrah in Ramadan equals Hajj.
Aisha, menstruating, left her Umrah for Hajj and later did Umrah from Tan'im with her brother; Umrah before Hajj is allowed for ever, its reward matching its cost and hardship.
Umrah rites as in Hajj: removing perfume, Tawaf of the Ka'bah and between Safa and Marwa, which may not be left, no relations before then, after which ihram ends.
A man came in a perfumed cloak; the Prophet received revelation, then told him to do in his Umrah as he does in his Hajj.
Aisha, regretting she returns with Hajj only, is sent behind her brother Abdur-Rahman on his mount to perform Umrah from at-Tan'im while the Prophet waits.
When the Prophet performs Umrah, making Tawaf, praying and going between Safa and Marwa, his companions guard him against the people of Mecca.
Under the treaty the Prophet returns next year for a three-day Umrah, Muslims walking briskly to show strength; Hamza's daughter is given to her aunt, and he marries Maimuna.
Aisha corrects Urwa's reading of the verse on Safa and Marwa: it came because Ansar held going between them sinful; Anas says they had dropped it as pre-Islamic.
